source.title: How Neural Networks Learn the Support is an Implicit Regularization Effect of SGD
source.authors: Pierfrancesco Beneventano; Andrea Pinto; Tomaso A. Poggio

record.tranche_reason: Tests how optimizer, batch size, and weight decay affect first-layer support selection and reports empirical results on synthetic targets, MNIST, and a pretrained ResNet feature head.
record.gate_note: Rows cover support selection, which is related to generalization but is distinct from held-out error. The paper reports comparable test losses across optimizers in one MNIST comparison, but gives no numerical values there. Cited generalization results in the background are not rows. Figure-only sweeps are included only where the text describes their direction.
record.test_reason: The study measures first-layer support identification, which none of V1–V8 names. Section 5.2 also reports comparable MNIST test losses across batch sizes, but does not establish a fixed epoch budget or a large-batch threshold, so this does not test V5 as stated. No adaptive optimizer comparison tests V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' main conclusion: mini-batch SGD and regularized GD promote first-layer support identification, with SGD's implicit effect increasing with the learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio. Their theoretical guarantees depend on architecture and oscillation conditions; ReLU networks and input directions unspanned by the data require qualifications, including the role of weight decay.
record.recipe_differences: Studies support identification and optimization dynamics, rather than the listed claims about memorization capacity, held-out generalization, or the training–test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and learning rate (the reported support-shrinking speed varies with η/b); optimizer choice (GD, SGD, and weight decay); initialization affects GD's solution more than SGD's after sufficient training. In the ReLU discussion, irrelevant-feature behavior depends on activation patterns and residuals.

fits_no_version.finding: Mini-batch SGD and weight decay shrink first-layer weights associated with irrelevant inputs; unregularized GD can represent the target while selecting support across later layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization choices affect where a network represents target support, with smaller batches promoting first-layer support identification in the studied settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The MNIST comparison reports comparable test losses while smaller batches improve first-layer support identification; the training budget is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First-layer support identification can differ across batch sizes despite comparable held-out loss.

record.problems: Many empirical support trends are shown in figures without numerical values; the paper does not provide uncertainty estimates for these results. The claim versions concern generalization and test error, while the main measured outcome is support identification. The practical CIFAR10 experiment uses a pretrained ResNet feature extractor with a trained MLP head, not an end-to-end CNN comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result rows were applicable. Cited findings about flat minima, generalization, and other papers were omitted because they are prior work, not results of this study. Figure-only weight visualizations without a textual outcome were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance on random-label test data.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Held-out error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including locality and initialization conditions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Held-out performance beyond a workload-dependent batch size under fixed epoch budgets, and recipes that remove its penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The observed support-selection findings remain valid findings; cannot_determine here refers to their inability to establish a listed claim version. Comparable MNIST test losses alone do not justify a V5 challenge.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness measurements and their relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring held-out accuracy.
